digest.component_or_area: codebase module-size governance and CI leading indicators
propositions: 46 of 435 src/rebar Python files exceed 700 LOC, with 7 files at or within 2 lines of the hard 800-LOC cap, creating an exhausted headroom condition across the repo.

The module-size indicator near_cap_count (currently 37 files within 10% of cap) exists in metrics but is invisible at runtime; it must be surfaced as a non-blocking CI warning in the Module-size gate to prevent future contributors discovering the problem too late.

pass1.py (800 LOC) can be split by extracting its container-pairing stage (CONTAINER_CRITERIA, _run_container, _timed_pairing, ~300 LOC) to a new container_stage.py module, with _submit_ctx relocated to generation.py to avoid circular dependencies between pass1 and the new module.

push.py (800 LOC) can be split by extracting its recovery cluster (_recover_dirty_merge, _recover_non_fast_forward, _merge_with_transport_retry, and six supporting functions, ~345 LOC) to push_recovery.py using late-binding core-parameter pattern to preserve monkeypatch sites.

All re-exports from source modules must be byte-identical to preserve attribute access in downstream consumers (orchestrator.py, provider_parity.py, push_state.py) and test-patch sites, with zero test file edits required.
The near-cap warning and both module splits must be documented in docs/architecture.md, and all changes must pass full CI-parity test suites with zero test count deltas against parent commits.
